D.1 RLOO control variate derivation

We derive the RLOO estimator (12) from the plug-in estimator (9). Using the chain rule, gmg_{m} from (7) decomposes into a score-function term and a pathwise term:

gm\displaystyle g_{m} =−wm​∇𝜽​log⁡p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)−∇𝜽wm.\displaystyle=-\,w_{m}\,\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*})-\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}w_{m}. (19)

Substituting into the plug-in estimator isolates the score-function component:

∇𝜽ℓq^plug-in=1M​∑m=1M[−wm(w¯M)q​∇𝜽​log⁡p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)−∇𝜽wm(w¯M)q].\displaystyle\widehat{\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\ell_{q}}^{\text{plug-in}}=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}\left[\frac{-w_{m}}{(\bar{w}_{M})^{q}}\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*})-\frac{\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}w_{m}}{(\bar{w}_{M})^{q}}\right]. (20)

Since 𝔼⁡[∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)]=0\mathbb{E}[\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*})]=0, we can subtract any baseline from the score-function coefficient −wm/(w¯M)q-w_{m}/(\bar{w}_{M})^{q} without changing the expected value, provided the baseline does not depend on 𝐳(m){{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}.

We use a leave-one-out approximation. Let w¯¬m=1M−1​∑j≠mwj\bar{w}_{\neg m}=\frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{j\neq m}w_{j}. Replacing wmw_{m} with w¯¬m\bar{w}_{\neg m} in the coefficient, the batch mean collapses to w¯¬m\bar{w}_{\neg m}, giving a surrogate coefficient of −(w¯¬m)1−q-(\bar{w}_{\neg m})^{1-q}. Subtracting this baseline yields the RLOO estimator (12).

Endpoint recovery.

At q=0q=0, the centered weight evaluates to wm−w¯¬mw_{m}-\bar{w}_{\neg m}, and the score-function term becomes −(wm−w¯¬m)​∇𝜽​log⁡p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)-(w_{m}-\bar{w}_{\neg m})\,\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}), exactly recovering the REINFORCE leave-one-out (RLOO) estimator standard in RLVR. At q=1q=1, the centered weight is wm/w¯M−1w_{m}/\bar{w}_{M}-1; since ∑m=1M(wm/w¯M−1)=0\sum_{m=1}^{M}(w_{m}/\bar{w}_{M}-1)=0, this acts as a self-normalizing baseline that strictly centers the importance weights across the batch.

D.1RLOO bias preservation, restated.

Under the assumptions of Theorem 6.1, the RLOO estimator (12) satisfies the same bias expansion as the plug-in estimator (9).

Proof.

The RLOO estimator (12) differs from the plug-in estimator (20) by subtracting (w¯¬m)1−q(\bar{w}_{\neg m})^{1-q} from the score-function coefficient wm/(w¯M)qw_{m}/(\bar{w}_{M})^{q} for each sample mm. Denoting sm=∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)s_{m}=\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}), the difference in expectations is

Δ\displaystyle\Delta =1M​∑m=1M𝔼[(w¯¬m)1−q​sm].\displaystyle=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}\mathop{\mathbb{E}}[(\bar{w}_{\neg m})^{1-q}\,s_{m}].

Since w¯¬m=1M−1​∑j≠mwj\bar{w}_{\neg m}=\frac{1}{M-1}\sum_{j\neq m}w_{j} is a function of {𝐳(j)}j≠m\{{{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(j)}\}_{j\neq m} only, and sm=∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳(m)∣𝐱∗)s_{m}=\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}) is a function of 𝐳(m){{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)} only, the independence of the i.i.d. samples gives

𝔼[(w¯¬m)1−q​sm]\displaystyle\mathop{\mathbb{E}}[(\bar{w}_{\neg m})^{1-q}\,s_{m}] =𝔼[(w¯¬m)1−q]⋅𝔼[sm]⏟= 0=0,\displaystyle=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}[(\bar{w}_{\neg m})^{1-q}]\cdot\underbrace{\mathop{\mathbb{E}}[s_{m}]}_{=\,0}=0,

where 𝔼[sm]=𝔼𝐳∼p𝜽[∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳∣𝐱∗)]=0\mathop{\mathbb{E}}[s_{m}]=\mathop{\mathbb{E}}_{{{{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}\sim p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}}}[\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*})]=0 is the standard score-function identity. Therefore Δ=0\Delta=0 and the two estimators have identical expectations for every MM. ∎

D.2 Endpoint recovery

D.2Endpoint recovery for GARL and PAFT.

Fix a supervised example (𝐱∗,𝐲∗)({{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}) with P𝛉>0P_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}>0.

  1. 1.

    GARL at q=0q=0 recovers Rao–Blackwellized REINFORCE [Williams, 1992, Zhou et al., 2026]:

    ∇𝜽ℓq^|q=0=g¯M=1M​∑m=1M(−wm​∇𝜽​log⁡p𝜽​(𝐳(m),𝐲∗∣𝐱∗)),\displaystyle\widehat{\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\ell_{q}}\big|_{q=0}=\bar{g}_{M}=\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m=1}^{M}\bigl(-w_{m}\,\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*})\bigr),

    which is unbiased for ∇𝜽ℓ0\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\ell_{0} by Equation 8. Each gmg_{m} marginalizes out the output 𝐲{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}} given 𝐳(m){{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)} analytically via wm=p𝜽​(𝐲∗∣𝐱∗,𝐳(m))w_{m}=p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*},{{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)}), rather than relying on a sampled output and binary reward.

  2. 2.

    GARL at q=1q=1 recovers the IWAE gradient estimator [Burda et al., 2015], a self-normalized importance sampling (SNIS) estimator for ∇𝜽​log​P𝜽\nabla_{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}\log P_{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}:

    ∇𝜽ℓq^|q=1=g¯Mw¯M=∑mwm​(−∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳(m),𝐲∗∣𝐱∗))∑mwm.\displaystyle\widehat{\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\ell_{q}}\big|_{q=1}=\frac{\bar{g}_{M}}{\bar{w}_{M}}=\frac{\sum_{m}w_{m}\,(-\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}))}{\sum_{m}w_{m}}.
  3. 3.

    PAFT at q=0q=0 reduces to posterior-resampled SFT scaled by P𝜽P_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}:

    ∇^PAFT|q=0=−w¯M⋅1K∑k=1K∇𝜽logp𝜽(𝐳(rk),𝐲∗∣𝐱∗).\displaystyle\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\big|_{q=0}=-\bar{w}_{M}\cdot\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(r_{k})},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}).

    The factor w¯M≈P𝜽\bar{w}_{M}\approx P_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}} downweights hard instances so aggressively that this endpoint is overly conservative in practice. Unlike the other three endpoints, it does not correspond to a standard method.

  4. 4.

    PAFT at q=1q=1 recovers the E-step of EM [Dempster et al., 1977] / TRICE [Phan et al., 2023]:

    ∇^PAFT|q=1=−1K∑k=1K∇𝜽logp𝜽(𝐳(rk),𝐲∗∣𝐱∗).\displaystyle\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\big|_{q=1}=-\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(r_{k})},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}).

    The instance weight (w¯M)1−1=1(\bar{w}_{M})^{1-1}=1 vanishes: all instances contribute equally, and the gradient is uniform SFT on approximate posterior samples.

Proof.

Each case follows by substituting q=0q=0 or q=1q=1 into the GARL estimator (9) or PAFT estimator (14) and simplifying (w¯M)0=1(\bar{w}_{M})^{0}=1. ∎

D.3 PAFT bias and variance

D.3PAFT has the same bias as GARL.

Under the assumptions of Theorem 6.1, 𝔼⁡[∇^PAFT]=𝔼⁡[∇^GARL]\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}]=\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}}] for all MM. In particular, the PAFT estimator has the same O⁡(q/M​P𝛉q+1)O(\nicefrac{{q}}{{MP_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}^{q+1}}}) bias as in Equation 11.

Proof.

Conditional on the prior samples pool={(𝐳(m),wm)}m=1M\mathrm{pool}=\{({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)},w_{m})\}_{m=1}^{M}, the factor (w¯M)1−q(\bar{w}_{M})^{1-q} is deterministic. The importance-resampled average satisfies

𝔼⁡[1K​∑k=1Kf⁡(𝐳(rk))|pool]=∑m=1Mwm∑jwj​f​(𝐳(m))=μ^SNIS,\displaystyle\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}f({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(r_{k})})\;\middle|\;\mathrm{pool}\right]=\sum_{m=1}^{M}\frac{w_{m}}{\sum_{j}w_{j}}\,f({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}}^{(m)})=\hat{\mu}_{\mathrm{SNIS}},

where f⁡(𝐳)=∇𝜽​log​p𝜽​(𝐳,𝐲∗∣𝐱∗)f({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}})=\nabla_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}\log p_{{\bm{\mathbf{\theta}}}}({{\bm{\mathbf{z}}}},{{\bm{\mathbf{y}}}}^{*}\mid{{\bm{\mathbf{x}}}}^{*}). Therefore

𝔼⁡[∇^PAFT∣pool]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool}] =−(w¯M)1−q⋅μ^SNIS\displaystyle=-(\bar{w}_{M})^{1-q}\cdot\hat{\mu}_{\mathrm{SNIS}}
=−(w¯M)1−q⋅∑mwm​fmM​w¯M\displaystyle=-(\bar{w}_{M})^{1-q}\cdot\frac{\sum_{m}w_{m}f_{m}}{M\bar{w}_{M}}
=1(w¯M)q⋅1M∑m(−wmfm)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{(\bar{w}_{M})^{q}}\cdot\frac{1}{M}\sum_{m}(-w_{m}f_{m})
=g¯M(w¯M)q=∇^GARL.\displaystyle=\frac{\bar{g}_{M}}{(\bar{w}_{M})^{q}}=\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}}.

Taking outer expectations by the tower property: 𝔼⁡[∇^PAFT]=𝔼⁡[∇^GARL]\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}]=\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}}]. ∎

D.4GARL has strictly lower variance than PAFT.

Under the same setup, 𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT)≥𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^GARL)\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}})\geq\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}}), with equality only when 𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT∣pool)=0\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool})=0 almost surely.

Proof.

By Proposition D.3, 𝔼⁡[∇^PAFT∣pool]=∇^GARL\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool}]=\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}}. The law of total variance gives

𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT)\displaystyle\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}) =𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(𝔼⁡[∇^PAFT∣pool])+𝔼⁡[𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT∣pool)]\displaystyle=\mathbf{Var}\bigl(\mathbb{E}[\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool}]\bigr)+\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool})\bigr]
=𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^GARL)+𝔼⁡[𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT∣pool)]⏟≥ 0,\displaystyle=\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{GARL}})+\underbrace{\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool})\bigr]}_{\geq\,0},

with equality iff 𝐕𝐚𝐫⁡(∇^PAFT∣pool)=0\mathbf{Var}(\hat{\nabla}_{\mathrm{PAFT}}\mid\mathrm{pool})=0 a.s. This holds when, for each pool realization, all resampled trajectories produce the same gradient  — e.g., when a single trajectory dominates the importance weights. In the non-degenerate case, the inequality is strict. ∎
